name: Night (Paragon Hag Family)
body:
Haunters of dreams, these dark hags capture the souls of the sleeping for trade on the outer planes. Their paragon hag families traffic with dark powers.

Family Spells: sleep (3rd), invisibility (6th), deep slumber (9th), phantasmal killer (12th), dismissal (15th), ethereal jaunt (18th)
Ritual Spells–Knowledge (Planes): dream (5th), nightmare (7th), hag’s ride* (9th), plane shift (11th), trap the soul (13th), gate (15th), extended dream voyage (17th), sympathetic* dominate monster (19th)
Family Powers: The marks of the soul trade remain on night hags’ kin.
Soul Armor (Su)

As long as you have at least one soul point available, you gain an armor bonus to AC equal to your Charisma modifier. This armor counts as a force effect and is effective against incorporeal touch attacks.

Soul Trade (Sp)

At 4th level, you can cast summon monster I as a spell-like ability by spending a soul point, but only to summon an evil creature. At 8th level, this effect improves to summon monster II. At 12th level, it improves further to summon monster III. At 16th level, it works as summon monster IV. And at 20th level, it works as summon monster V. Even when summoning monsters from a lower-level list, you never summon more than 1 monster per casting this way.

Sleep Paralysis (Su)

At 8th level, when you damage a creature with your claws, you may spend a soul point to paralyze them for 1d4+1 rounds unless they succeed at a Will save. You may use this ability on sleeping creatures without spending a soul point. The DC of the save is 10 + 1/2 your paragon hag level + your Charisma modifier.

Soul Heart (Su)

At 12th level, you gain a bonus equal to your Charisma bonus (if any) on all Saving Throws.

Hagridden (Su)

At 16th level, your claws and spells deal 1 point of Constitution drain to sleeping or paralyzed targets. You may gain 10 temporary hit points when this drain takes effect, and these temporary hit points last until you next recover spells.

Legendary Family

Upon reaching 20th level, when a humanoid creature of at least 10 HD dies within 30 feet of you, you may bind its soul into your soul focus as an immediate action. You may not store more than one soul in your focus at a time, but while a particular soul is in your focus, you may consume it as a soul point (or as a free action simply to dispose of it). After it’s consumed, the soul can only be returned to life with miracle or wish.
